concept.title: Math and Equations
concept.abstract: This section covers Mathematical Equations — quantitative expressions that cannot be represented accurately through prose alone — and five scenarios: a block equation, an inline equation, an equation in a table cell, an equation in a list item, and an equation in a procedure step. The converter maps native <math> (MathML) markup to <foreign> containing embedded MathML; image-based equations map to <image> with a required <alt> element carrying the equation's accessible text description.

conbody.p: Mathematical equations communicate quantitative relationships that cannot be expressed accurately through prose alone. They are commonly used in engineering, scientific, financial, and technical documentation to represent formulas, calculations, algorithms, and symbolic expressions.
The mathematical equation can be inserted as:

ul.li: MathType objects - MathType is a third-party equation editor that embeds equations as OLE (Object Linking and Embedding) binary objects.
Image-based equations - An equation represented as a PNG, EMF, or other image file — whether inserted directly or produced by a screenshot — carries no mathematical structure.
Reference-based equations – An equation is stored separately as an external MathML file, which can be reused or maintained outside the topic.

conbody.p: In HTML, mathematical content may be authored as native MathML, rendered as images, or represented using LaTeX syntax through client-side rendering libraries.

The converter evaluates how each equation is represented in the HTML source before determining the generated DITA output. Native MathML is preserved and converted to the corresponding DITA MathML structure. Image-based equations are treated as standard images, while LaTeX expressions are converted only when the mathematical markup is available in the HTML source before conversion. The quality of the generated DITA output depends directly on the format in which mathematical content is authored.
